cells.tense: You are sitting in the deep place, and your feet are under the table.
cells.ask: Write down the one thing that matters most right now, before you can explain why. Keep the page, and read it back tomorrow.
cells.core:
You can follow a thought down past where most people stop, and you come back with something. Not a theory — a way of seeing that was already there, now with words on it. Telling what matters before you can say why isn't a trick you pull off. It's how you work.

The depth isn't a mood you visit. Sitting with something long enough for its shape to show is what tells you which hours are worth the ones you have, and people around you feel the difference. Notice tomorrow what you stop reaching for. The quiet isn't the absence of work. It's the work, and you're in it now.

cells.verb: Going all the way down into your own thinking until the pattern shows.

cells.tense: You are digging toward a bottom you haven't found, and you won't come up until you do.
cells.ask: Say the pattern you've found out loud, to one person, in plain words. Then stop and leave it with them.
cells.core:
You're heading for the bottom of it, and the going is getting steeper. Out ahead, the whole thing finally makes sense, and you're living there while this hour waits for you to come back up. Thinking has turned into the thing you do when you don't want to arrive.

What's underneath is not more depth. It's the move you haven't made: saying what you already see, in words, to somebody who can hear it. That's the shape you keep circling, and a circle stays a circle until you hand it to someone. Say the one pattern you're sure of. Let it out of your head and into the room, then let the room be a place you come back to.

cells.tense: You stopped going below the surface, and the shallows have held.
cells.ask: Ask one person a question you actually care about, and let them answer it fully. Curiosity handed back and forth is the whole act.
cells.core:
The deep place is still there. You're not using it. Going down got harder than staying up, so you learned to stay where the water's thin — and it worked. You can still follow a thought, still spot what matters. You've just stopped letting it matter.

What brings it back isn't discipline. It's contact. Whatever you know about seeing clearly came through somebody once — a person who showed you, a conversation that handed it over. Go find one. Ask someone a question whose answer you can't predict. That isn't a method for you; it's the current running back through the wire. Curiosity with a person in it. That's the first step down.

cells.tense: You are reading what matters in this room right now, and you call it observation.
cells.ask: Name one thing you noticed in someone today — a mood, a shift, a tone — and say 'I caught that' as you say it.
cells.core:
You read people and situations quickly. You know what matters in a room before anyone has said it, and you move on it, quietly, all the time. You'd call it paying attention, or being observant, or having a read on things — as if that were something anyone could do.

It isn't. This runs at full strength without your name on it. What you catch keeps arriving as a simple fact about the world, and the fact that you're the one catching it gets left off. Naming it doesn't make you grand. It makes it land instead of float. Pick one thing you caught today. Say that you caught it. The one who noticed is you.
